name: Self-Distillation Without Labels
analogy: Think of it as a junior analyst and a calm senior version of themselves. The junior sees a slightly distorted copy of a chart, the senior sees a different distorted copy, and the junior must describe the chart the way the senior would. The senior is simply a slow-moving average of the junior's past selves, so the two keep each other steady.

steps.title: Make two altered copies of each window
steps.description: Each unlabelled window of bars is copied twice, and each copy is changed a little in a way that should not change its meaning: a touch of noise, a small rescaling, a few bars masked. The model is going to be asked to see through these changes.
steps.inExample: One 48-bar MNQ window becomes view A with small noise added and view B with 15 percent of its bars masked.

steps.title: Send one copy to the student and one to the teacher
steps.description: Two networks with the same shape read the copies. The student is the one being trained. The teacher is not trained directly; its weights are a slow-moving average of the student's weights over time.
steps.inExample: The student reads view A and the teacher reads view B, each producing a summary of 64 numbers.

steps.title: Compare their summaries
steps.description: Both networks output a normalised summary vector. The gap between the student's summary of one copy and the teacher's summary of the other copy is measured. A small gap means the model sees the same underlying window through both distortions.
steps.inExample: The two summaries point in nearly the same direction, with a similarity of 81 percent at the start of training.

steps.title: Update only the student
steps.description: The student is adjusted to make its summary closer to the teacher's. No label and no price direction is involved at all. The teacher receives no gradient; it is the fixed target for this step.
steps.inExample: The student's weights move a small step so that its view-A summary lines up better with the teacher's view-B summary.

steps.title: Let the teacher drift toward the student
steps.description: After each update the teacher's weights move a tiny fraction of the way toward the student's. Because the teacher changes slowly, it gives a stable target and discourages the trivial cheat of making every summary identical.
steps.inExample: Each step the teacher takes about 1 percent of the student's weights, so it trails the student by roughly a hundred updates.

steps.title: Keep the student's summaries for later use
steps.description: After many repetitions, the student's summary of a window is a general-purpose description. It can be fed to a classifier or a forecaster trained on a small set of labels, or used to cluster market states.
steps.inExample: The final 64-number summary of a window gets a similarity of 93 percent with the summary of its own distorted copy, and 12 percent with an unrelated window.

useFor.example: Learning summaries from years of unlabelled MNQ bars, then training a small direction classifier on a few months of labels.
Grouping windows by their summaries to discover recurring sessions, such as grinding trends and choppy rotations.
Flagging windows whose summary sits far from every cluster as unlike recent history.
Producing summaries for price windows and for FinBERT news sentiment scores, so both can feed one downstream model.

avoidWhen: You already have plenty of reliable labels for the exact task; training on the labels directly is simpler and usually better.
You cannot name distortions that leave the meaning of a window unchanged; if the changes alter what the window means, the model learns the wrong thing.

example.scenario: A researcher pretrains on a year of unlabelled 5-minute MNQ windows. Afterwards, they feed today's window to the student and read its summary, then check how stable that summary is under distortion.

input.summary: A window of 48 five-minute bars described by rescaled features, plus two distorted copies used during training.

fields.name: window length
fields.meaning: Four hours of trading described to the model.

fields.name: features per bar
fields.meaning: Return, range, body share, wick balance, volume and similar measures, all rescaled.

fields.name: distortion in view A
fields.meaning: A little random noise added to every feature.

fields.name: distortion in view B
fields.meaning: Some bars hidden so the model must infer them from the rest.

fields.name: teacher update rate
fields.meaning: How far the teacher moves toward the student after each update.

output.summary: A summary vector for the window and similarity checks that show whether the summary is stable and informative.

fields.name: summary vector
fields.meaning: The learned description of the window that other models can use.

fields.name: similarity between the two distorted copies
fields.meaning: How alike the summaries of the two copies are; 100 percent would be identical.

fields.name: similarity to an unrelated window
fields.meaning: How alike the summary is to that of a different window, which should be low.

example.reading: A high similarity between copies and a low similarity to other windows says the summary is stable and still distinguishes windows. It does not say the summary predicts direction. The next step is to train a small direction model on the summaries over walk-forward folds and check that it beats the same model on raw features after costs.
